intelligence.enrichment: Iron develops brown deposits only when it is in contact with both air and water. Dry air without water and water shielded from air do not produce brown deposits; rusting can be prevented by painting, oiling, greasing, or applying zinc on iron. The presence or absence of both air and water determines whether iron rusts, and protective coatings prevent rusting by blocking contact. The learner correctly applies this rule: Iron develops brown deposits only when it is in contact with both air and water. Dry air without water and water shielded from air do not produce brown deposits; rusting can be prevented by painting, oiling, greasing, or applying zinc on iron. Iron rusts when it touches either air or water; one of them is enough.
